fixes.explanation: The poor never come up in this verse, friend. God's complaint is aimed at the shepherds themselves. He says they “…only feed themselves!” And verse 4 adds that they ruled the flock “with violence and cruelty.” (Ezekiel 34:4)

That's the one. God says, “You have not strengthened the weak, healed the sick, bound up the injured, brought back the strays, or searched for the lost.” That's five jobs on the list, and none of them got done. I think this one hurts, because these were the sheep who needed care the most.
YES. God says, “Behold, I Myself will search for My flock and seek them out.” The shepherds didn't search, so the LORD steps in and does it Himself. The search belongs to Him.
The elders of Israel aren't named in this promise. God says, “Behold, I Myself will search for My flock and seek them out.” The LORD takes the search on Himself.

Guarding isn't what God describes here. He asks, “Is it not enough for you to feed on the good pasture? Must you also trample the rest of the pasture with your feet?” The leftover pasture gets trampled. The word that fits is trample.

That's the one. God says, “I will appoint over them one shepherd, My servant David, and he will feed them.” David was tending sheep when God sent for him (1 Samuel 16:11-13), and God had chosen him as king (1 Samuel 16:1). So a shepherd feeding the flock is a good name to hear.
